original_question: Let K be compact and assume the weak and norm Borel sigma-algebras on C(K) differ, so Bo(C(K), w) ≠ Bo(C(K)). Must there exist a norm-discrete subset of C(K) that is not weak-Borel, that is, does not belong to Bo(C(K), w)?
target_in_paper: Problem 2.4 (Burke-Pol) in §2.2 (“Borel σ-algebras”). The paper states: “Let K be compact such that Bo(C(K), w) ≠ Bo(C(K)). Is there a norm discrete subset of C(K) which does not belong to Bo(C(K), w)?” ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the official hypothesis and conclusion almost verbatim: it assumes Bo(C(K), w) ≠ Bo(C(K)) and asks whether there must be a norm-discrete subset of C(K) lying outside Bo(C(K), w). ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
missing_details: State that K is a compact Hausdorff space; the paper globally assumes all topological spaces are Hausdorff and uses “compact” as shorthand for a compact topological space. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

Specify that C(K) is being treated in the paper’s real Banach-space setting; the global conventions say that only real Banach spaces are considered. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

Make explicit that Bo(C(K)) denotes the Borel σ-algebra for the norm (uniform) topology on C(K), while Bo(C(K), w) denotes the Borel σ-algebra for the weak topology; this comparison is the setup of §2.2 and display (2.1). ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

Clarify that “norm-discrete” means discrete with respect to the norm topology on C(K). The paper leaves this implicit in the phrase “norm discrete subset of C(K).” ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
refined_question: Let K be a compact Hausdorff space, and let C(K) be the real Banach space of continuous real-valued functions on K with the supremum norm. Assume that the Borel σ-algebra of the weak topology on C(K) is strictly smaller than the Borel σ-algebra of the norm topology, i.e. Bo(C(K), w) ≠ Bo(C(K)). Must there exist a subset A ⊆ C(K) that is discrete for the norm topology and satisfies A ∉ Bo(C(K), w)?
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 2.4 exactly, rather than a broader neighboring question. Section 2.2 first sets up the relevant chain of σ-algebras on C(K) in display (2.1), then immediately asks Problem 2.4 in essentially the same words as your draft. The only paper-faithful additions needed to make the question fully stand-alone are the global conventions that all spaces are Hausdorff, only real Banach spaces are considered, and that Bo(C(K)) refers to the norm-topology Borel σ-algebra when no other topology is specified. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
